USMLE-style practice · Pathology

Antioxidant enzyme reaction

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An experimental antioxidant enzyme reduces the concentration of superoxide in reoxygenated cells. Chemical analysis shows that its immediate products include hydrogen peroxide and molecular oxygen. Which enzyme catalyzes the reaction described in this experiment?

  1. Superoxide dismutase
  2. Catalase
  3. Glutathione peroxidase
  4. Myeloperoxidase
  5. NADPH oxidase
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Superoxide dismutase

Superoxide dismutase converts superoxide to hydrogen peroxide and oxygen.

Understanding the options

Superoxide dismutase
Superoxide dismutase converts superoxide to hydrogen peroxide and oxygen.
Catalase
Catalase breaks down hydrogen peroxide rather than directly dismutating superoxide.
Glutathione peroxidase
This enzyme reduces peroxides using glutathione.
Myeloperoxidase
Myeloperoxidase uses hydrogen peroxide in antimicrobial oxidant formation.
NADPH oxidase
NADPH oxidase generates superoxide rather than removing it.
